newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-DUTCH GOALKEEPER SEGERS FAMED FOR ERRATIC STYLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DUTCH GOALKEEPER SEGERS FAMED FOR ERRATIC STYLE.

text.p: Dutch-born goalkeeper Hans Segers, who goes on trial here on Tuesday charged with match-fixing, was prized as a great shot-stopper but was also capable of making dreadful mistakes on the pitch.
Segers, who played more than 300 times for Wimbledon, was renowned for his willingness to leave the penalty area in an attempt to clear the ball or make a challenge.
The 35-year-old Dutchman, now playing for first division Wolverhampton Wanderers on a non-contract basis, was even known to turn up in the opposing team's goalmouth when Wimbledon had a corner kick.
"He was mad as a March hare -- he would let in a simple goal and then save five brilliant shots," said one club insider.
"He was loved by the fans. He was an eccentric goalkeeper but a brilliant shot stopper. We never had any problems with him off the field."
Otherwise he was a model of consistency, missing only five game in seven seasons at the south London club.
Segers played for six years with fellow defendant John Fashanu but played no part in the so-called "Crazy Gang", a collection of players known for their wild antics.
He kept very much to himself off the pitch and made few public appearances, although while at Wimbledon he did found a tie-making firm.
Segers was born in the Dutch city of Eindhoven and started with local club PSV, but he made few appearances and moved to English side Nottingham Forest in 1984.

Chances there were also infrequent and he made only 67 appearances in four years before moving to Wimbledon in 1988 for 125,000 pounds. He replaced keeper Dave Beasant, who was sold to Newcastle after the team's 1-0 F.A. Cup win over Liverpool.
Hans Johannes Cornelius Segers was born on October 30, 1961 in Eindhoven. He is married and has two children.
